subject: Recap: Redwood x Aurora Payments discovery — cost / TCO framing
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aurorapay.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@aurorapay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood discovery — cost focus

Hi Dev / Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — helpful to see Redwood's runtime and the levers you mentioned. Quick recap from our side and a couple clarifying Qs: 

- Primary pain: our inference spend is the single biggest line item for the payments bot (chat + receipts summarization).
- Current monthly baseline: ~20M inference tokens, several short sessions (median 120 tokens) + occasional long-ticket summaries (~6k tokens).
- Current vendor bill (inference only): ~$4,800/mo. Our CFO wants to get below $2,500/mo or show a 12-month ROI if we stay above that.
- Key asks: how much can batching/caching/quantization realistically bring down per-token costs for our workload? What tradeoffs on latency/quality?

Questions:
1) Can you share a simple TCO example showing hosted vs dedicated vs private for our profile?
2) Any quick ways to guarantee budget predictability for Q3?

Thanks — happy to loop procurement if we can get a preliminary workbook.

Best,
Alex
Director of Product, Aurora Payments

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood discovery — cost focus

Alex — great to talk yesterday. Pushing the quick TCO sketch below and a suggested set of next steps so you can share with procurement/CFO. I appended assumptions so numbers are traceable.

TL;DR: For the workload you described (20M inference tokens/month, short median session length, sporadic long summaries), we estimate a 50–60% reduction in monthly spend compared to your current vendor if you adopt Redwood's batching + KV prefix caching + int8 quantized model variant on Dedicated capacity. Hosted can achieve similar unit economics for POC but Dedicated gives stronger predictability and peak SLAs.

High-level example (monthly):
- Baseline: 20,000,000 inference tokens / month. Current vendor cost: $4,800/mo (as you reported).
- Redwood hosted estimate (mix of hosted + caching): modeled unit cost $0.00012 / token -> $2,400/mo before discounts.
- Redwood dedicated estimate (small reserve + autoscaling + optimized kernels): modeled unit cost $0.00007 / token -> $1,400/mo.
- Estimated one-time POC engineering effort (Redwood + Aurora): 2 engineer-weeks (integration + telemetry), we can run POC in your dev account or in a shared test pool.

How the savings happen (lever breakdown):
1) Batching: continuous batching with a 20ms max latency window increases GPU utilization for short requests — effective per-token cost reduction of ~20–30% on generation-heavy flows.
2) KV prefix caching: for the bot's FAQ and receipts templates we expect 35–50% of tokens to be cacheable (session prefixes & repeated system prompts) — that directly removes token billable work.
3) Quantization and model selection: switching to an int8-quantized variant of the same model architecture reduces memory footprint and allows denser packing — shaving another ~10–15% from unit cost with negligible quality loss on short-turn tasks.
4) Request routing: routing longer summary jobs to a higher-throughput node (spot/dedicated mix) to avoid latency-sensitive queueing, while keeping short interactions on low-latency pool.

Tradeoffs & assumptions:
- Latency: target p50 latency for short sessions remains <120ms across Dedicated; batch window tuned to 20ms. If you need p95 <200ms under burst, we recommend a small warm reserve (adds ~10% to committed cost).
- Quality: quantized variant tested on representative prompts showed <1.5% delta on the metrics your team cares about (utterance-level correctness). We will include those evals in the POC.
- Billing: caching reduces billable tokens only for cached prefixes; full summaries still charge per token.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I will share a filled TCO worksheet by end of day Friday with the assumptions used (attached).
2) If procurement okays, we propose a 4-week POC: week 0 onboarding + instrumentation (2 engineer-weeks), weeks 1–3 live traffic mirror and telemetry. POC deliverables: token-level cost dashboard, latency percentiles, sample quality evals.
3) Discuss committed capacity pricing if Aurora signs a 12-mo reserve (we can propose blended committed + burst pricing to hit your $2,500/mo target).

Action items: 
- Dev (me): send the worksheet + sample contract language.
- Marissa: prepare a short SOW draft for a 4-week POC.
- Rishi: will follow up with a quick note on quantized model variants and sample evals.

I attached a starter worksheet (Aurora_TCO_Worksheet.xlsx) with a simple scenario generator. Review and tell us which scenarios you want modeled.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks and look forward to moving quickly.

Marissa
